full_judgment:
Al-haj Md Serajuddin as the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. (number not stated) of 1998 renumbered as Title Suit No. 234 of 2003 in the Additional Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka praying for declaration of title and recovery of khash possession on removing the construction standing on the suit property. His case, in short, is that he purchased the land of 'Ka' schedule to the plaint with two storied building, garage, different plants situated on SA Dag No. 10 of Mouza-Kakrail under previous Lalbagh Police Station now Ramna within Dhaka Collector ate from Syed Farooq Mirja, son of Syed Fakrul Hasan Mirja in 1971. After purchase, the plaintiff got his name mutated and had been paying taxes regularly. While the plaintiff was abroad, the 'Ka' schedule was wrongly declared abandoned property. Having come to know of the aforesaid fact, the plaintiff filed an application to the Government of Bangladesh and the Government having been satisfied released the suit property in favour of the plaintiff and issued memo dated 19-6-1983 from the office of defendant No. 3 but defendant No. 1 did not return the land shown in schedule 'Kha' to the plaint. Consequently, the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 53 of 1988 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Fourth Court, Dhaka, which was decreed on 17-12-1988. After that, the plaintiff requested defendant Nos. 1 and 2 to deliver 'Kha' schedule land to him on a number of dates from 26-3-1989 up to 3-5-1997 and lastly, on 8-7-1997 but defendant No. 1 did not vacate or deliver 'Kha' schedule land to the plaintiff. As such the plaintiff issued legal notice upon defendant No. 1 on 1-9-1997. But defendant No. 1 did not pay any heed to the said request made by the plaintiff and consequently, the suit was filed. Along with plaint, the plaintiff filed sketch map showing position of the garage. During pendency of the suit, the sole-plaintiff died and his heirs were substituted as the plaintiffs. 

 19. Having gone through the record, the judgment delivered in Title Suit No. 53 of 1988 and the evidence of PW 1 given in Title Suit No. 234 of 2003, we find that the plaintiff had been out of possession of the suit land ('Kha' schedule land) according to their admission from 1974. The present suit for declaration of title and recovery of khash possession was filed in 1998. Therefore, the suit is hopelessly barred by limitation. The plaintiff was required to file the suit for declaration of title and recovery of possession within 12 years from the alleged date of dispossession but they have been failed to do so and, as such, they are not entitled to get a decree for recovery of possession. 

 "The last but not the least point that has been noticed by this Court at the time of hearing of the appeal is that there is no averment in the plaint of plaintiffs dispossession from the suit land within twelve years of bringing the suit which is for recovery of khas possession. Notwithstanding this, both the trial Court and the lower appellate Court concurrently found that the plaintiffs had never been in possession of the suit land. In such circumstances, the suit was not maintainable. On this ground alone the plaintiffs suit was liable for dismissal." 

 23. On consideration of the cases referred to above, it appears that in a suit for declaration of title and recovery of khash possession, the plaintiffs in addition to proving their title to the suit land must prove that the suit has been filed within 12 years from the alleged date of dispossession. In the case in hand, the plaintiffs miserably failed to prove that the suit has been filed within 12 years from the alleged date of dispossession. 

 24. In the light of the findings, we are of the view that the High Court Division erroneously decreed the suit for declaration of title and recovery of khash possession.
